question.text: A letter lock consists of three rings with 15 different letters. If \(\mathrm{N}\) denotes the number of ways in which it is possible to make unsuccessful attempts to open the lock, then

options.text: N is the product of two distinct prime numbers.
\(\mathrm{N}\) is the product of three distinct prime numbers.

solution.text:
Hint : Number of unsuccessful attempts \(=15^3-1=3374=2 \times 1687=2 \times 7 \times 241\)
Divisible by 482
\(\mathrm{N}\) is the product of three distinct prime number
